title: Frontend: Factorial of a number
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Factorial of a number. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution(n). For integers 0..100, compute exact factorial using BigInt and return its decimal string. Reject other inputs with Invalid n.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Define 0! as one, validate an integer input, and multiply iteratively from two through n.
alternativeApproaches: Return the number of trailing decimal zeros using factors of five rather than constructing the entire factorial.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: 0; 1; ordinary positive input.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
